A headless worker's usage counts as its item's work, so cost ID and cost --rework SP show it, whether its worktree is orchestrator-made on work/<id> or an Agent-tool subagent's; usage.md says how a headless worker in an orchestrator-made worktree is attributed; land's 'landed with no work rows' warning tells a late row (the worker's session still open or its sidecar undistilled) from a missing one, stops for a worker whose rows exist, and names a store a session end left undelivered (unpushed).
